newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish cabinet clears free trade pact with Latvia.
newsitem.headline: Polish cabinet clears free trade pact with Latvia.

text.p: The Polish government on Tuesday approved a free trade agreement with Latvia, which brings the Baltic republic closer to membership of the Central European Free Trade Agreement.
The government said in a statment that the two countries would abolish customs duties on most industrial products when the accord becomes effective.
Some tariffs would continue to apply for the so-called sensitive products, such as farm goods, textiles, steel, oil products and cars, but they would gradually be phased out, the statement said.

Latvia still needs to sign a free trade agreement with Hungary and join the World Trade Organisation to be eligible to enter CEFTA, which now includes the Czech Republic, Hungary, Poland, Slovakia and Slovenia.
On July 1, Romania is to become the sixth member of CEFTA, which was created in 1992 to revive trade among former members of the defunct Soviet bloc.
